description: Provider capability matrix. The app reads this file at runtime and exposes a capability to learners only when status is 'verified' AND learnerVisible is true. Everything else falls back to the next lower tutor tier (ultimately Tier 1: validated recorded clips). Change a status only after the evaluation described in docs/capability-matrix.md has been completed and recorded here.

capabilities.stt: Speech-to-text: transcribe a learner's spoken question in the teaching language (tutor Tier 2).
capabilities.tts: Text-to-speech: speak generated explanations aloud (tutor Tier 3).
capabilities.translation: Machine translation between English and the teaching language.
capabilities.pronunciation_scoring: Automatic scoring of a learner's spoken English against a model.
capabilities.llm_dialogue: LLM understanding and generation in the language (intent classification for Tier 2, generated explanations for Tier 3).

device-web-speech.name: Device speech engine (Web Speech API on the learner's phone)

entries.notes: Vendor documentation (checked 2026-10-26) lists isiZulu (lang_code 'zul', code-switched isiZulu) for the synchronous transcription endpoint POST /api/v2alpha/transcribe/sync/file. The adapter is implemented but has not been run against real learner audio. Required before 'verified': word error rate on the Tier 2 question set recorded by 10+ adult isiZulu speakers on entry-level Android phones, in quiet and noisy settings, judged by a native speaker.

Vendor documentation (checked 2026-10-26) lists Sesotho (lang_code 'sot'). The docs note that word-level timings and confidence are not available for Sesotho. Verify that the model handles South African Sesotho orthography and speech (not only Lesotho Sesotho) before use. Same evaluation protocol as isiZulu.
Advertised by the vendor. Not integrated. The app never machine-translates learner-facing content: all translations come from validated lesson content.
Advertised by the vendor. Not integrated. The app never machine-translates learner-facing content.
No text-to-speech product was found in the vendor documentation on 2026-10-26. Re-check before planning Tier 3.

No pronunciation assessment product was found in the vendor documentation. The app uses self-check with model audio instead and records such practice as 'practised', never 'mastered'.

Adapter implemented for Tier 2 intent classification (output is restricted to a fixed list of intent IDs, so no generated text reaches learners) and Tier 3 explanation drafting. isiZulu generation quality for adult literacy explanations has not been evaluated by native speakers. Tier 3 also needs a verified isiZulu TTS voice, which does not exist in this matrix.
As for isiZulu. Evaluation must check South African Sesotho orthography (for example 'dijo', not 'lijo'; 'kg' not 'kh').
English output is only ever shown to facilitators (text view, marked 'AI-generated, unverified'). Learners never receive English text in place of their teaching language.
Entry-level Android phones do not normally ship an isiZulu voice. Not integrated. The app never falls back to an English device voice for isiZulu content.
Entry-level Android phones do not normally ship a Sesotho voice. Not integrated.
Device English voices vary in accent and quality and are not a validated pronunciation model. English model audio must be recorded and reviewed like all other audio.
Browser speech recognition availability for isiZulu on Android Chrome is device- and account-dependent and sends audio to a third party without our controls. Not integrated.
As for isiZulu. Not integrated.
